raw: {"analysis":"Response ZKJ correctly identifies the migration as irreversible and designs a rollback plan that relies on feature flagging rather than schema reversal, which is the only safe approach. Response CLS makes a critical error by proposing a 'transactional rollback' for an explicitly irreversible migration, and also suggests running the migration on a 'production replica first' which conflates staging with production replicas. Both responses correctly sequence the legacy parser update before introducing new status codes, but ZKJ's treatment of the shared library (defaulting to an adapter pattern to avoid the approval bottleneck) is more practically grounded.","verdict":"ZKJ"}
